description: A Second Brain is an external, searchable memory built from your own notes, ideas, and links - usually kept in a note-taking app. The idea is one concrete methodology within the older field of personal knowledge management: instead of holding everything in your head, you store knowledge in a structured way and retrieve it when you need it. The CODE principle (Capture, Organize, Distill, Express) puts the weight on the last step: notes are supposed to turn into output. The limit is real: collecting is not understanding. An archive full of unread clippings is not a second brain, just a full basement.
example: You read an article about learning strategies and save the core idea in your own words in your note-taking app, linked to your notes on memory and habits. A year later you search for 'learning' - and find in seconds what your head forgot long ago.
